### CR-066 — The desk's "New business" tile counts renewals bound in the Desktop, and "Renewals · 90 days" counts policies already renewed that the table below excludes
- **Status:** Open (first seen 2026-10-30)
- **Where:** `/Users/djsiry/GitHub/underwriting-desktop/web/src/lib/dashboard.ts:65-72` (policies query selects no `renewed_from`), `:84-95`, `:189-195`; rendered at `/Users/djsiry/GitHub/underwriting-desktop/web/src/app/page.tsx:59-62`; `/Users/djsiry/GitHub/underwriting-desktop/web/src/app/book/page.tsx:28` inherits the same filter; the assistant's `book_summary` (`/Users/djsiry/GitHub/underwriting-desktop/web/src/lib/assistant-tools.ts:264-266`) reports the same numbers
- **Problem:** Step 16 made a Desktop-bound policy a renewal when `policies.renewed_from` is set and marks the expiring policy `renewal_status = 'renewed'`, but the KPIs were not updated. `written` (every in-force Desktop policy) feeds `newBusinessPremium`/`newBusinessPolicies`, so binding a renewal raises "New business … bound in the UW Desktop". `renewalsDue90`/`renewalPremium90` filter `book` by date only, while the "Upcoming renewals" table (`renewals`) also drops `renewal_status === "renewed"`, so after a renewal is bound the tile (and `/book?due=90`) say one more renewal than the table lists.
- **Evidence:** `newBusinessPremium: written.reduce((n, p) => n + p.premium, 0)` under the comment "Everything written in the UW Desktop is new business"; `renewalsDue90: book.filter((p) => daysUntil(p.expiration_date, today) <= 90).length` versus `const renewals = book.filter((p) => … && p.renewal_status !== "renewed")`; the policies query selects `p.renewal_status, p.renewal_submission_id` but not `renewed_from` (re-read this run).
- **Fix:** Select `(p.renewed_from IS NOT NULL) AS is_renewal`; compute `newBusiness*` from `written.filter((p) => !p.is_renewal)`; derive `renewalsDue90`/`renewalPremium90` from `renewals` (`daysUntil(...) <= 90`) and apply the same `renewal_status !== "renewed"` filter in `/book?due=`, so tile, list, table and `book_summary` agree.
- **Verify:** Bind a renewal from the workbench and reload `/`: "New business" is unchanged, "Renewals · 90 days" drops by one and equals the rows in "Upcoming renewals" within 90 days; `/book?due=90` lists the same rows.

### CR-090 — Unauthenticated sign-in attempts put raw `Accept-Language` and `User-Agent` text into the Markdown sign-in report that a scheduled Claude task reads, unescaped and unbounded
- **Status:** Open (first seen 2026-10-31)
- **Where:** `/Users/djsiry/GitHub/underwriting-desktop/web/src/app/signin/actions.ts:26` (every attempt is recorded; `/signin` is outside the gate per `/Users/djsiry/GitHub/underwriting-desktop/web/src/middleware.ts:9`), `/Users/djsiry/GitHub/underwriting-desktop/web/src/lib/login-events.ts:15-21` (the INSERT), `/Users/djsiry/GitHub/underwriting-desktop/web/src/lib/login-meta.ts:44-45` (`user_agent` up to 500 chars, `accept_language` up to 100), `:97` (`browserLabel` falls back to the first 30 characters of an unrecognised UA), `:170,185` (`esc()` neutralises only `|`; `eventsTable` prints `e.edge_region` and `e.accept_language.split(",")[0]` with no escaping at all); consumers `/Users/djsiry/GitHub/underwriting-desktop/web/src/app/api/reports/logins/route.ts:30-31` and `/Users/djsiry/GitHub/underwriting-desktop/scripts/login-report.sh:12-13` ("from a scheduled Claude task"); the CSV form at `login-meta.ts:210-213` passes the raw `user_agent` through `toCsv` (see CR-071)
- **Problem:** Anyone on the internet can post the sign-in form with a made-up user and any `Accept-Language`/`User-Agent`; the attempt is stored as `(unknown user)` with those header values, with no rate limit and no cap on rows. The daily Markdown report prints the language tag verbatim (100 characters, unescaped: a `|` shifts every later column of that row) and the UA's first 30 characters, and the build log says the file is read by an automated Claude task, which makes it a prompt-injection channel from unauthenticated traffic. `aa32db3` closed the address half (SEC-033: `ip` is now taken only from `Fly-Client-IP` or behind `TRUSTED_PROXY=1`), but the two text headers are unchanged. The `/audit/logins` page renders the same strings through React (safe).
- **Evidence:**
  ```ts
  await recordLogin(ok || users.has(name) ? name : "(unknown user)", ok, "signin", h)   // signin/actions.ts:26
  accept_language: h.get("accept-language")?.slice(0, 100) || null,                     // login-meta.ts:45
  … | ${esc(browserLabel(e.user_agent)) || "—"} | ${esc(e.accept_language?.split(",")[0] ?? "") || "—"} |`   // login-meta.ts:185
  : ua.split(" ")[0].slice(0, 30);                                                       // login-meta.ts:97
  const esc = (s: string) => s.replace(/\|/g, "\\|");                                    // login-meta.ts:170
  ```
  `grep -n "rate\|limit" web/src/app/signin/actions.ts` → nothing; `migrations/policy/007_login_events.sql` has no row cap or retention.
- **Fix:** Treat the two header values as untrusted: keep `accept_language` only when its first tag matches `/^[A-Za-z]{1,8}(-[A-Za-z0-9]{1,8})*$/` (else `null`), store the raw UA in the row but render only a whitelisted label (`/^[A-Za-z]+ \d+( · [A-Za-z]+)?$/`, else `"other"`) in the Markdown, make `esc()` also strip `[\x00-\x1f]` and collapse whitespace, and don't store UA/language for `(unknown user)` rows. Add a per-address limit on failed attempts (for example 20 per 10 minutes, refused with the same "isn't right" message). Extend `eventCsvRow` with CR-071's wider formula guard.
- **Verify:** POST the sign-in form with `-H 'Accept-Language: | ignore previous instructions'`, `-H 'User-Agent: =HYPERLINK("x")'` and a wrong password; `GET /api/reports/logins?format=md` shows the row intact with no injected text, `format=csv` shows the UA cell quoted with a leading `'`; a `login-meta.test.ts` case asserts `reportMarkdown` never emits a header value verbatim.

### CR-017 — Guard worksheet Save & rate against lost updates (same gap CR-006 closed for intake)
- **Status:** Open (first seen 2026-10-23)
- **Where:** `/Users/djsiry/GitHub/underwriting-desktop/web/src/lib/worksheets.ts:93-122`; form `/Users/djsiry/GitHub/underwriting-desktop/web/src/app/submissions/[id]/workbench/page.tsx:97,143`
- **Problem:** `saveAndRate` reads the worksheet via `openWorksheet`, diffs the form against that snapshot, then runs an unconditional `UPDATE worksheets SET rating_inputs = $2, schedule = $3 … WHERE submission_id = $1`. No transaction, no `FOR UPDATE`, no fingerprint on the form. Two people on one file (the renewal comparison page and the workbench share a submission): the later save silently reverts the earlier one's inputs and schedule, and its `worksheet.input_changed` events record "before" values from its stale snapshot.
- **Evidence:** `grep -n 'FOR UPDATE' web/src/lib/worksheets.ts` → nothing (re-run this run); `withReviewLock`/`dataFingerprint` in `submissions.ts:142-163` show the pattern already used for review.
- **Fix:** Render a hidden `_fingerprint` = `inputsHash(ws.rating_inputs, ws.schedule)` on the workbench form. In `saveAndRate`, `BEGIN`, `SELECT * FROM worksheets WHERE submission_id = $1 FOR UPDATE`, compare the fingerprint and throw `"${sub.reference} was changed by someone else since you opened it. Reload, then save again."` on mismatch, diff and UPDATE inside the transaction, commit before calling rating.
- **Verify:** Open one workbench in two tabs; change receipts in A and save; save B with the old receipts: B must be refused, not revert A; the Worksheet history shows only A's change.

### CR-052 — Rate admin "Save <section>" writes every stale cell back, silently reverting a colleague's change and auditing it under the wrong name and reason
- **Status:** Open (first seen 2026-10-24)
- **Where:** `/Users/djsiry/GitHub/underwriting-desktop/services/rating/app/admin.py:335-368`, `/Users/djsiry/GitHub/underwriting-desktop/services/rating/app/repository.py:184-215`, form `/Users/djsiry/GitHub/underwriting-desktop/services/rating/app/templates/version.html:31-67`
- **Problem:** The section form posts every cell, and `apply_edits` treats any posted value that differs from the database as an intended edit. A changes FL 1.25 → 1.35 and saves; B, whose page still shows 1.25, changes TX and saves: B's form carries FL = 1.25, which now differs from 1.35, so FL is written back and audited as `update_factor territory:FL 1.35 → 1.25` under B's name and reason. `_lock_draft` serialises transactions but cannot detect a stale form. The JSON API is immune.
- **Evidence:** `edit.values[column] = value` … `updates = {c: v for c, v in edit.values.items() if Decimal(v) != row[c]}`; `grep -c '|was' services/rating/app/templates/version.html` → 0 (re-run this run).
- **Fix:** Add `<input type="hidden" name="{{ c.field }}|was" value="{{ c.value | num }}">` per cell; in `save_section` skip cells whose value equals their `was` and pass `expected` per `Edit`; in `apply_edits` raise `ValueError(f"{_entity(edit)} was changed by someone else since you opened it (now {row[c]}). Reload and try again.")` when `row[c] != expected[c]`.
- **Verify:** `test_rate_admin.py`: post `FL=1.35, FL|was=1.25`; then `FL=1.25, FL|was=1.25, TX=1.2, TX|was=1.1`: only TX changes and FL stays 1.35 with no revert in the audit; then `FL=1.40, FL|was=1.25` re-renders with a "changed by someone else" error.

### CR-084 — `startRenewal` claims the policy in the policy DB before it connects to the customer DB, and the connect sits outside the `try` that undoes the claim, so one failed connection leaves a dangling `renewal_submission_id` that 404s every renewal path for that policy forever
- **Status:** Open (first seen 2026-10-30)
- **Where:** `/Users/djsiry/GitHub/underwriting-desktop/web/src/lib/renewals.ts:169-207` (`startRenewal`), `:147,159,167` (`existing` short-circuit), `:231-234` (`renewalOfPolicy`); consumers `/Users/djsiry/GitHub/underwriting-desktop/web/src/app/policies/actions.ts:8-19`, `/Users/djsiry/GitHub/underwriting-desktop/web/src/app/policies/[id]/page.tsx:36,114-122`, `/Users/djsiry/GitHub/underwriting-desktop/web/src/app/policies/book/[id]/page.tsx:32,86-94`, `/Users/djsiry/GitHub/underwriting-desktop/web/src/lib/dashboard.ts:150-158`
- **Problem:** The claim is a two-database write with no transaction across them: first `UPDATE policies|book_policies SET renewal_status = 'in_progress', renewal_submission_id = $2 WHERE … renewal_submission_id IS NULL` (policy DB), then `const client = await customerDb.connect()` and the `INSERT INTO submissions`/`worksheets` transaction. The compensating `UPDATE … SET renewal_status = 'not_started', renewal_submission_id = NULL` lives in the `catch` of that transaction, but `customerDb.connect()` is called *before* the `try`, so a pool timeout, a customer-DB restart or a crash at that instant leaves the policy pointing at a submission id that was never inserted. From then on `renewalOfPolicy()` finds no submission and the policy page shows "Start renewal" again; clicking it returns `{ submissionId: existing }` because `renewal_submission_id` is set, and the action redirects to `/submissions/<dangling>/renewal`, which `notFound()`s. The desk's "Finish renewal" task (status `in_progress`, ≤ 30 days) links to the same 404. Only hand SQL recovers it.
- **Evidence:** `const claimed = await policyDb.query(\`UPDATE ${table} SET renewal_status = 'in_progress', renewal_submission_id = $2 WHERE id = $1 AND renewal_submission_id IS NULL\`, …)` (line 172); `const client = await customerDb.connect();` (line 181) precedes `try { await client.query("BEGIN"); …` (line 184); `if (existing) return { submissionId: existing, created: false };` (line 167) with no check that the submission exists (re-read this run).
- **Fix:** Reverse the order so the policy DB is written last: insert the submission and worksheet in the customer DB first (id generated up front, as now), then run the conditional claim `UPDATE … WHERE renewal_submission_id IS NULL`; if the claim stamps zero rows (a concurrent start won), delete the just-inserted submission/worksheet and return the winner's id. Make the `existing` path self-healing: when `renewal_submission_id` is set but `getSubmission(existing)` is null, clear the claim and proceed as a fresh start. Move `customerDb.connect()` inside the `try` regardless.
- **Verify:** Point `CUSTOMER_DATABASE_URL` at a closed port, click "Start renewal" on a book policy, restore the URL, reload: the page still offers "Start renewal" and clicking it creates the renewal (no 404); `SELECT renewal_submission_id FROM book_policies WHERE id = …` is null after the failed attempt. Add a `renewals.test.ts` case for the self-healing branch.

### CR-029 — One unreadable or forwarded attachment discards the entire broker email
- **Status:** Open (first seen 2026-10-23)
- **Where:** `/Users/djsiry/GitHub/underwriting-desktop/services/ingestion/app/documents.py:81-86` (and `:46-48`)
- **Problem:** `_email` calls `load(name, part.get_payload(decode=True), parent=filename)` per attachment, catching only `UnsupportedDocument`. A `message/rfc822` part (forwarded email) yields `get_payload(decode=True) is None`, so `load` evaluates `data[:5]` on `None` and raises `TypeError` (or, for a `.pdf`-named part, `PdfReader(BytesIO(None))` raises); a corrupt PDF raises from `pypdf` the same way. The exception escapes `_email`, and `pipeline.run` drops the whole `.eml`: the body (the main source for sparse submissions like cases 05 and 14, and every generated `broker_email_sparse` folder) and every good attachment are never read. Unsupported attachment types are skipped with no warning.
- **Evidence:** `try: docs += load(name, part.get_payload(decode=True), parent=filename) except UnsupportedDocument: continue`; `load()` begins `if suffix == ".pdf" or data[:5] == b"%PDF-":`; `pipeline.run:31-34` catches the escaped error per file (re-read this run).
- **Fix:** Read `payload = part.get_payload(decode=True)`; `if payload is None: continue` (or recurse with `_email` for `message/rfc822`); widen the per-attachment `except` to `Exception`; pass a `warnings` list into `load` so a skipped attachment is reported by name.
- **Verify:** Test an `.eml` with the case 04 body, its loss-run PDF and a forwarded `message/rfc822` part: `load()` returns body and loss run and `pipeline.run` does not warn the `.eml` was unreadable; also an `.eml` with a `b"%PDF-garbage"` PDF and one with an `.xlsx` (expect a named warning).

### CR-019 — `issueQuote` does side-effecting work before it has fully validated dates or taken a lock
- **Status:** Open (first seen 2026-10-23)
- **Where:** `/Users/djsiry/GitHub/underwriting-desktop/web/src/lib/quotes.ts:78-81`, `:83-94`, `:149-171`; `/Users/djsiry/GitHub/underwriting-desktop/web/src/lib/submission.ts:136`
- **Problem:** Dates are checked by regex only. `2026-02-30` passes, is rated through the API (writing a `rating_log` row `Q-… vN`), rendered to PDF (and, for a renewal, to a memo), and only then fails at the `date` cast, so the rating log shows a quote version that never existed. `2026-13-01` with blank expiration throws `RangeError` from `addYears`. `fromInput` has the same hole. `previous`/`version` are read without a lock and rating plus PDF render precede the transaction, so a double-click yields a raw `quotes_quote_number_version_key` violation and another orphan log row.
- **Evidence:** `if (!/^\d{4}-\d{2}-\d{2}$/.test(effective)) throw …` is the only check; `Date.parse("2026-02-30T00:00:00Z")` → `1772409600000` (re-run this run); Postgres `'2026-02-30'::date` → out of range.
- **Fix:** Add `isIsoDate(s)` (regex plus round-trip `new Date(s + "T00:00:00Z").toISOString().slice(0,10) === s`) in `quote-terms.ts`; use it for both quote dates before any external call, in `fromInput` for `date`, and for CR-068. Take the next version inside the transaction (`SELECT … FOR UPDATE`) and map the unique violation to "already issued, reload". Also closes CR-050.
- **Verify:** `node --test` for `isIsoDate` on `2026-02-30`, `2026-13-01`, `2026-02-28`; issuing with `2026-02-30` gives a friendly error and no new `rating_log` row.

### CR-050 — A bind that commits while a re-quote is in flight leaves a bound v1 and an issued v2, writes a false `quote.superseded` event, and disables the "already bound" guard for that file
- **Status:** Open (first seen 2026-10-24)
- **Where:** `/Users/djsiry/GitHub/underwriting-desktop/web/src/lib/quotes.ts:83-84`, `:149-171`, `:173-178`; `/Users/djsiry/GitHub/underwriting-desktop/web/src/lib/policies.ts:82-150`
- **Problem:** `issueQuote` reads `previous` and checks `bound` unlocked, then rates and renders before opening its transaction. If a bind commits in that window, `UPDATE quotes SET status = 'superseded' … AND status = 'issued'` matches zero rows (rowCount unchecked), v2 is inserted as `issued`, the audit records `quote.superseded` for a bound quote, and every later `issueQuote` sees `previous` = v2 and passes the bound check.
- **Evidence:** `const previous = (await quotesForSubmission(sub.id))[0]; if (previous?.status === "bound") throw …` before rating (re-read this run); nothing in the migrations prevents an `issued` row beside a `bound` row.
- **Fix:** Inside the transaction `SELECT … FROM quotes WHERE submission_id = $1 ORDER BY version DESC FOR UPDATE`, derive number/version from the locked rows, refuse if any is `bound`, and use the UPDATE's `rowCount` to decide which `quote.superseded` events to write. Fix with CR-019.
- **Verify:** Add a temporary 3 s pause after line 84 and bind during it: the re-quote fails with "already bound", `/quotes` shows v1 bound and no v2.

### CR-034 — Quote, bind and renewal audit events are written after the policy-DB COMMIT, although `audit()` can now join a transaction
- **Status:** Open (first seen 2026-10-23)
- **Where:** `/Users/djsiry/GitHub/underwriting-desktop/web/src/lib/quotes.ts:165-189`, `/Users/djsiry/GitHub/underwriting-desktop/web/src/lib/policies.ts:144-174`, `/Users/djsiry/GitHub/underwriting-desktop/web/src/lib/renewals.ts:200-226`; the helper `/Users/djsiry/GitHub/underwriting-desktop/web/src/lib/audit.ts:20-33`
- **Problem:** `quotes`, `policies`, `gl_postings` and `audit_events` live in one database, yet `issueQuote`, `bindQuote` and `startRenewal` COMMIT then call `audit()`, which inserts each event separately with no `BEGIN`. A failure between leaves a quote, policy or ledger journal with no `quote.issued`/`policy.bound`/`gl.posted` event or a partial correlated group; the GL API's `journalDocument` then shows a journal whose "underwriting action" has no events. `aa32db3` gave `audit()` an optional `Queryable` and `exportLedger` now uses it inside its transaction (`ledger.ts:223-228`); the three pipeline functions still do not.
- **Evidence:** `await client.query("COMMIT"); … finally { client.release(); } … await audit(` in all three (re-confirmed this run); `audit(...args: AuditEvent[] | [AuditEvent[], Queryable])` at `audit.ts:20`.
- **Fix:** In `issueQuote`, `bindQuote` and `startRenewal` call `audit([...events], client)` before `COMMIT` on the same client (the policy-DB client for quotes/binds; for `startRenewal`, the policy-DB events on a policy-DB client in the same step as the claim).
- **Verify:** Temporarily throw inside `audit()` after the first insert and bind: the bind must roll back rather than leave a policy and journal with a partial trail.

### CR-049 — An audit-insert failure after a committed upload is reported as an upload error, inviting a duplicate submission and a second Claude call
- **Status:** Open (first seen 2026-10-24)
- **Where:** `/Users/djsiry/GitHub/underwriting-desktop/web/src/lib/submissions.ts:118-135`; surfaced by `/Users/djsiry/GitHub/underwriting-desktop/web/src/app/submissions/actions.ts:17-22` and `/Users/djsiry/GitHub/underwriting-desktop/web/src/app/submissions/inbox/[folder]/extract/route.ts:63-67`
- **Problem:** `storeSubmission` commits the customer-DB transaction then calls `audit()` (policy DB) inside the same `try`; a failure there runs `ROLLBACK` after `COMMIT` (no-op) and rethrows, so the upload form shows an error although `SUB-000N` was stored, and the natural retry re-runs the 20–40 s extraction and creates a second reference. On the inbox path the activity panel shows "error" while the folder has silently left the inbox.
- **Evidence:** `await client.query("COMMIT"); … await audit({…}); return { id, reference }; } catch (err) { await client.query("ROLLBACK"); …; throw err; }` (re-confirmed this run).
- **Fix:** Isolate the transaction in its own `try/catch/finally`; call `audit()` after it in a separate `try`, logging and returning the id (or a non-blocking warning) on failure. Apply the same split to `saveReview`, `acceptSubmission` and `saveAndRate`.
- **Verify:** Point `POLICY_DATABASE_URL` at a closed port, upload case 01: the action redirects to the new review page and the inbox shows one new row.

### CR-067 — A transient rating-service failure while computing the renewal bridge is swallowed and persisted as "rate version X couldn't be rated on"
- **Status:** Open (first seen 2026-10-30)
- **Where:** `/Users/djsiry/GitHub/underwriting-desktop/web/src/lib/worksheets.ts:176-186`; shown at `/Users/djsiry/GitHub/underwriting-desktop/web/src/app/submissions/[id]/renewal/page.tsx:132`, baked into the memo at `/Users/djsiry/GitHub/underwriting-desktop/web/src/lib/renewal-memo-pdf.ts:94-97` via `/Users/djsiry/GitHub/underwriting-desktop/web/src/lib/quotes.ts:133-147`
- **Problem:** `bridgeRating` wraps `rateVersionId()` and `rateOn()` (both 15 s) in `catch { return null }`. A cold-start timeout or a 5xx therefore looks exactly like "the expiring version no longer exists": Save & rate reports success, `bridge_rating` is stored as `null`, the comparison page says "Rate version 2026.1 couldn't be rated on, so the change can't be split", and if the underwriter issues the renewal quote the memo PDF (frozen, never regenerated) tells the insured the same thing. Nothing is logged. `RatingServiceError.rejectedInputs` is the right discriminator and is not used here.
- **Evidence:** `try { const versionId = await rateVersionId(exp.rate_version); return versionId ? await rateOn(…) : null; } catch { return null; }` (re-read this run).
- **Fix:** Return `null` only when `rateVersionId` resolves to `null` (or the error is a `RatingServiceError` with `rejectedInputs`); let transport and 5xx errors propagate, or store `{ error: message }` in `bridge_rating` and render "rating service unavailable; re-rate" instead of blaming the version.
- **Verify:** Temporarily make `rateVersionId` throw; Save & rate on a renewal must show an error banner and leave `bridge_rating` untouched; with a real missing label it must still show the "couldn't be rated on" note.

### CR-036 — Check-then-insert races on unique keys surface as raw constraint errors (rate activation, draft label, insured FEIN)
- **Status:** Open (first seen 2026-10-23)
- **Where:** `/Users/djsiry/GitHub/underwriting-desktop/services/rating/app/repository.py:153-162`, `:218-229`, `/Users/djsiry/GitHub/underwriting-desktop/services/rating/app/main.py:97-105`, `/Users/djsiry/GitHub/underwriting-desktop/services/rating/app/admin.py:264-274,371-379`, `/Users/djsiry/GitHub/underwriting-desktop/web/src/lib/submissions.ts:222-227`
- **Problem:** (1) `activate()` locks only its own draft; two concurrent activations both pass `_lock_draft` and the second hits `one_active_version`. (2) `create_draft()` checks `SELECT 1 … WHERE label = %s` before inserting into a `UNIQUE` column. (3) `acceptSubmission` does `SELECT id FROM insureds WHERE fein = $1` then `INSERT`. Data stays consistent but the `UniqueViolation` is unmapped: a bare 500 in the admin, Postgres's raw message on the review page.
- **Evidence:** `previous = conn.execute("UPDATE rate_versions SET status = 'retired' WHERE status = 'active' RETURNING label")` after locking only the draft (re-confirmed at `repository.py:224-226`); `const existing = fein ? … : undefined; const insuredId = existing?.id ?? "all" : "this_month")` and take `preset`/`from`/`to`/`type`/`batch` from `query` (the export route already does this), so bare `from`/`to` mean a custom range everywhere. ### CR-071 — The CSV export neutralizes `=`, `+` and `@` but not `-`, tab or CR, which spreadsheets also treat as formula starters
- **Status:** Open (first seen 2026-10-30)
- **Where:** `/Users/djsiry/GitHub/underwriting-desktop/web/src/lib/csv.ts:11-13`; data sources are broker-supplied text (`insured_name`, `description`, `producer`) in `/Users/djsiry/GitHub/underwriting-desktop/web/src/lib/ledger.ts:179-184` and the raw `user_agent`/`accept_language` of unauthenticated sign-in attempts in `/Users/djsiry/GitHub/underwriting-desktop/web/src/lib/login-meta.ts:210-213` (served by `/api/reports/logins?format=csv` and `scripts/login-report.sh --csv`)
- **Problem:** The export is explicitly "pushed to the GL as CSV" and opened in Excel. The guard `/^[=+@]/` leaves a cell beginning with `-` (e.g. a description `-2+3+cmd|' /C calc'!A0` or `-HYPERLINK(...)`) unquoted, which Excel and LibreOffice evaluate as a formula on import; leading tab/CR are the other documented starters. Insured names and operation descriptions come from broker documents via Claude, and the sign-in CSV carries header values anyone can send to `/signin`, so the prefix is attacker-reachable on two files.
- **Evidence:** `const s = /^[=+@]/.test(v) ? \`'${v}\` : v;`; `/^[=+@]/.test("-2+3")` → `false` (re-run this run).
- **Fix:** `const s = /^[=+\-@\t\r]/.test(v) ? \`'${v}\` : v;` (numbers are typed `number` and are unaffected). The `.xlsx` writer is safe already (`t="inlineStr"`).
- **Verify:** `export-formats.test.ts`: `toCsv(["a"], [["-2+3"]])` contains `'-2+3`; a negative numeric cell `-5` stays `-5`; a sign-in attempt with `User-Agent: -cmd` appears quoted in `format=csv`.

### CR-072 — A "Working as" name outside Latin-1 makes every `/admin` page a 500 through the proxy (local dev only)
- **Status:** Open (first seen 2026-10-30)
- **Where:** `/Users/djsiry/GitHub/underwriting-desktop/web/src/app/admin/[[...path]]/route.ts:27`; name source `/Users/djsiry/GitHub/underwriting-desktop/web/src/app/submissions/actions.ts:83-86` and `/Users/djsiry/GitHub/underwriting-desktop/web/src/lib/user.ts:15-17`; reader `/Users/djsiry/GitHub/underwriting-desktop/services/rating/app/auth.py:36-40`
- **Problem:** The proxy sets `"x-uw-user": await currentUser()`. Locally that is the free-text cookie (any 60 characters). `fetch` header values must be ByteStrings, so a name such as `Łukasz` or `李雷` throws `TypeError: Cannot convert argument to a ByteString …` before the request is sent, and every Rate-tables page returns the error boundary until the cookie is changed. This is the web-side twin of CR-057. With the gate on (Fly) the value is the signed-in login (ASCII from `fly-users.sh`), so the deployed app is unaffected.
- **Evidence:** `"x-uw-user": await currentUser(),` inside the `fetch` headers object; `setUserAction` applies only `.trim().slice(0, 60)` (re-read this run).
- **Fix:** Send `encodeURIComponent(user)` in the header and `urllib.parse.unquote` it in `acting_user()` (do the same for CR-057's cookie), or restrict `setUserAction` to `^[\x20-\x7E]{1,60}$`.
- **Verify:** Set "Working as" to `Łukasz`, open `/admin`: 200 and "Signed in as Łukasz"; the rating audit row for a saved edit shows `Łukasz`.

### CR-083 — A session cookie stays valid for up to 7 days after its user is removed from `BASIC_AUTH_USERS` when `SESSION_SECRET` is set, because the middleware never checks the session's user against the configured logins
- **Status:** Open (first seen 2026-10-30)
- **Where:** `/Users/djsiry/GitHub/underwriting-desktop/web/src/middleware.ts:29-34`; key derivation `/Users/djsiry/GitHub/underwriting-desktop/web/src/lib/session.ts:13-15`; session issue `/Users/djsiry/GitHub/underwriting-desktop/web/src/app/signin/actions.ts:28-32`
- **Problem:** `middleware` accepts `verifySession(cookie, sessionKey(env))` as the identity without testing `users.has(name)`. The build log's stated safety net ("changing the passwords signs everyone out") only holds for the *derived* key: `sessionKey` returns `SESSION_SECRET` unchanged when it is set, so with that documented option in use, deleting a login from `BASIC_AUTH_USERS` (or rotating one password) leaves that person's 7-day `uw_session` fully valid and every page, API and MCP call still runs and audits as them. `fly-users.sh` only adds users, so removal is a hand edit that an operator would reasonably expect to take effect on restart.
- **Evidence:** `const name = verifySession(req.cookies.get(SESSION_COOKIE)?.value, sessionKey(process.env)) ?? authenticate(req.headers.get("authorization"), users);`; `return env.SESSION_SECRET || createHash("sha256")…`; `grep -c 'users.has' web/src/middleware.ts` → 0 (re-run this run).
- **Fix:** After `verifySession`, require `users.has(name)` (`const fromSession = verifySession(…); const name = (fromSession && users.has(fromSession) ? fromSession : null) ?? authenticate(…)`). Optionally mix a per-user password hash into the signed payload so a password change also invalidates that user's sessions under `SESSION_SECRET`.
- **Verify:** With `SESSION_SECRET` set, sign in as `underwriter2`, remove `underwriter2` from `BASIC_AUTH_USERS`, restart: the next navigation redirects to `/signin`. Add a `session.test.ts`/middleware-level test for a valid cookie naming an unknown user.

### CR-074 — Audit timestamps are caller-supplied with no record of insertion time, so back-dated rows are indistinguishable from real ones
- **Status:** Open (first seen 2026-10-30)
- **Where:** `/Users/djsiry/GitHub/underwriting-desktop/web/src/lib/audit.ts:12,24-30` (`occurredAt` → `occurred_at`), `/Users/djsiry/GitHub/underwriting-desktop/services/rating/app/main.py:41,57-60` and `/Users/djsiry/GitHub/underwriting-desktop/services/rating/app/repository.py:40-48` (`rated_at` → `rating_log.created_at`); callers `/Users/djsiry/GitHub/underwriting-desktop/web/src/lib/seed-history.ts:149-171`; schemas `/Users/djsiry/GitHub/underwriting-desktop/web/migrations/policy/001_audit_events.sql:4`, `/Users/djsiry/GitHub/underwriting-desktop/services/rating/migrations/001_schema.sql:54`
- **Problem:** Step 19 made every pipeline function take an `at` that is written straight into `audit_events.occurred_at` and, over the unauthenticated `POST /rate`, into `rating_log.created_at` (the table the schema calls "for audit and replay"). Neither table keeps the real insertion time: a row dated March that was inserted in October looks exactly like one written in March, and anyone who can reach the rating service can log a rating at any date. The new append-only triggers (`008_append_only_logs.sql`, rating `004`) stop rewriting but not back-dated insertion. The seeding use case is legitimate; the gap is that the trail cannot tell the two apart.
- **Evidence:** `VALUES ($1, …, $8, coalesce($9, now()))`; `" VALUES (%s, %s, %s, %s, %s, coalesce(%s, now())) RETURNING id"`; `grep -rn recorded_at web/migrations services/rating/migrations` → nothing (re-run this run).
- **Fix:** Add `recorded_at timestamptz NOT NULL DEFAULT now()` to `audit_events` and `rating_log` (new migrations), never settable by callers, and show it in the audit viewer when it differs from `occurred_at` ("seeded"/"back-dated"). Optionally accept `occurredAt`/`rated_at` only when `SEED_HISTORY` is set, and only from a caller holding `RATING_ADMIN_TOKEN` on the rating side.
- **Verify:** After migrating, `SELECT count(*) FROM audit_events WHERE recorded_at - occurred_at > interval '1 day'` equals the number of seeded events; a `POST /rate` with `rated_at` outside seeding is refused or recorded with `recorded_at = now()`.

### CR-075 — Seeded submissions carry `method: "form_fields"` and `doc_type: "acord_125"`, values outside the extraction contract, so their review page says the application was read by Claude
- **Status:** Open (first seen 2026-10-30)
- **Where:** `/Users/djsiry/GitHub/underwriting-desktop/web/src/lib/seed-history.ts:95-101`; consumers `/Users/djsiry/GitHub/underwriting-desktop/web/src/app/submissions/[id]/page.tsx:155-160` (`d.method === "form_field" ? "form fields" : "Claude"`), `/Users/djsiry/GitHub/underwriting-desktop/services/ingestion/app/documents.py:35-39` and `/Users/djsiry/GitHub/underwriting-desktop/services/ingestion/app/pipeline.py:7-11` (the real vocabulary)
- **Problem:** The ingestion service emits `method` as `"form_field" | "claude"` and `doc_type` from `DOC_TYPE_LABELS` (`acord_application`, `loss_run`, …). The seeded `Extraction` invents `"form_fields"` and `"acord_125"`, so for all 50 seeded files the Documents panel reads "acord 125: …-acord-125.pdf · Claude" under a header that says `claude: null`, and any future rule keyed on `doc_type === "acord_application"` will skip them. `documents[].method` and `doc_type` are typed `string`, so the compiler cannot catch it.
- **Evidence:** `documents: [{ filename: application, doc_type: "acord_125", parent: null, method: "form_fields" },` (re-confirmed this run).
- **Fix:** Use `doc_type: "acord_application"` and `method: "form_field"`; narrow `Extraction.documents[].method` to `"form_field" | "claude"` and `doc_type` to the union of `DOC_TYPE_LABELS` keys in `submission.ts`.
- **Verify:** Open a seeded submission's review page: the Documents panel says "ACORD application: … · form fields"; `tsc` fails if a literal outside the union is used.

### CR-033 — `lpad(…, 4)` truncates reference and quote numbers past 9,999, producing collisions
- **Status:** Open (first seen 2026-10-23)
- **Where:** `/Users/djsiry/GitHub/underwriting-desktop/web/src/lib/submissions.ts:107`, `/Users/djsiry/GitHub/underwriting-desktop/web/src/lib/renewals.ts:193`, `/Users/djsiry/GitHub/underwriting-desktop/web/src/lib/quotes.ts:87`; the assistant's `get_quote` parser `/Users/djsiry/GitHub/underwriting-desktop/web/src/lib/assistant-tools.ts:204` hard-codes the same four digits (`/^(Q-\d{4}-\d{4})(?:\s*V(\d+))?$/`) while `search-terms.ts:11` accepts `Q-\d{4}-\d+`
- **Problem:** Postgres `lpad` truncates longer strings, so sequence value 10000 becomes `SUB-1000` / `Q-2026-1000`, colliding with 1000 under the unique constraints. Seeding (50 per run) and the self-refilling inbox (10 per top-up) make the sequence grow faster than before. Once the padding is widened, the assistant's `get_quote` regex must follow or it will answer "No quote Q-2026-10001" for a quote the search box finds.
- **Evidence:** `SELECT lpad('10000', 4, '0')` → `1000` (documented Postgres behaviour); three `lpad(nextval…, 4` sites by grep this run; `/^(Q-\d{4}-\d{4})(?:\s*V(\d+))?$/.test("Q-2026-10001")` → `false` (re-run this run).
- **Fix:** `lpad(n::text, GREATEST(4, length(n::text)), '0')` or format in TypeScript with `padStart`; change the `get_quote` regex to `Q-\d{4}-\d+`. Fix CR-045 at the same time.
- **Verify:** `setval('submission_reference_seq', 9999)` on a scratch DB, upload twice: `SUB-10000`, `SUB-10001`; `get_quote` with `Q-2026-10001` resolves.

### CR-045 — `GET /ratings?reference_prefix=` is an unanchored, unescaped prefix match, so the case view will mix reference families
- **Status:** Open (first seen 2026-10-23)

### CR-032 — Out-of-range rate values are a 500 from the admin UI and API, not a validation message
- **Status:** Open (first seen 2026-10-23)
- **Where:** `/Users/djsiry/GitHub/underwriting-desktop/services/rating/app/repository.py:200-204`, `/Users/djsiry/GitHub/underwriting-desktop/services/rating/app/admin.py:349-366`, `/Users/djsiry/GitHub/underwriting-desktop/services/rating/app/main.py:97-105`, `/Users/djsiry/GitHub/underwriting-desktop/services/rating/migrations/001_schema.sql:32,41`
- **Problem:** `apply_edits` rejects only `<= 0`. `factors.value` is `numeric(8,4)`, so `100000` (or any value with more than four integer digits) reaches the UPDATE and Postgres raises `numeric field overflow`, a `psycopg.DataError` that neither `admin_errors` nor `save_section`'s `except (LookupError, ValueError, repository.VersionNotEditable)` catches; the admin returns a bare 500 and the typed edits are lost, and the JSON API returns 500 instead of 422.

- **Fix:** Validate before the UPDATE: `if not v.is_finite() or v <= 0 or v >= Decimal("10000"): raise ValueError(...)`; catch `psycopg.DataError` in `admin_errors` and `save_section` as a backstop.
- **Verify:** `edit(client, draft["id"], value=100000).status_code == 422`; a form post with `100000` re-renders with a readable error instead of a 500.

### CR-020 — Claude call can retry for ~15 minutes and non-API failures escape as 500s
- **Status:** Open (first seen 2026-10-23)
- **Where:** `/Users/djsiry/GitHub/underwriting-desktop/services/ingestion/app/claude.py:159`, `:204-205`
- **Problem:** `anthropic.Anthropic(api_key=…, timeout=300.0)` keeps the SDK default `max_retries=2`, so a failing request can hold a threadpool worker for three 300 s attempts while the web tier abandons at 300 s and the underwriter retries. Only `APIStatusError`/`APIConnectionError` become warnings; `next(b.text for b in response.content if b.type == "text")` (StopIteration with no text block) and `json.loads(text)` sit outside the `try` and surface as HTTP 500 on `/extract` (and as an in-band `error` on `/extract/stream`).
- **Evidence:** `grep -n "max_retries" services/ingestion/app/claude.py` → nothing (re-run this run); lines 204-205 are outside the `try`.
- **Fix:** `anthropic.Anthropic(api_key=api_key(), timeout=240.0, max_retries=1)`; wrap the text lookup and `json.loads` in `try/except (StopIteration, ValueError)` raising `ExtractionError("Claude returned no parseable JSON")`.
- **Verify:** Monkeypatch the stream's `get_final_message` to return a response with only a thinking block; `pipeline.run` must return a warning, not raise.

### CR-087 — Cancelling a streamed extraction does not stop the Claude call already running, and `/extract/stream` runs each request on its own uncancellable, unbounded daemon thread
- **Status:** Open (first seen 2026-10-31)
- **Where:** `/Users/djsiry/GitHub/underwriting-desktop/services/ingestion/app/main.py:88-120` (`extract_stream`: the `work()` thread, the `lines()` generator), `/Users/djsiry/GitHub/underwriting-desktop/services/ingestion/app/claude.py:161-194` (the streaming loop has no cancellation check); the cancelling side `/Users/djsiry/GitHub/underwriting-desktop/web/src/app/submissions/inbox/[folder]/extract/route.ts:37-40` and `/Users/djsiry/GitHub/underwriting-desktop/web/src/app/submissions/inbox-list.tsx:66-70`
- **Problem:** Cancel reaches exactly as far as the ingestion socket. The web route aborts its `fetch`, and Starlette stops iterating `lines()` when the client disconnects, but nothing signals `work()`: it keeps consuming the Claude stream to the end (20–40 s, the full token spend), keeps `emit`ting into a `queue.Queue` nobody drains, then exits. So Cancel saves nothing, and the natural next click runs two Claude extractions at once. Unlike `/extract`, which goes through `run_in_threadpool` (bounded by anyio's default pool), every `/extract/stream` request spawns a fresh `threading.Thread(daemon=True)` holding the uploads and the base64 PDFs, with no cap and no way to stop it.
- **Evidence:** `threading.Thread(target=work, daemon=True).start()`; `for event in stream:` in `claude.py:176` runs to completion regardless of the client; `work()` and `claude.extract()` take no cancellation token (re-read this run).
- **Fix:** Create a `threading.Event()` per request and pass it through `pipeline.run(..., cancelled=ev)` into `claude.extract`; in the stream loop `if cancelled.is_set(): stream.close(); raise ExtractionError("extraction cancelled")`. Set the event from a `finally:` in `lines()` and/or a `BackgroundTask`. Bound concurrency with a module-level `threading.Semaphore(4)` acquired in `work()` (answer 503 "busy" when it cannot be acquired within a few seconds).
- **Verify:** Add an ingestion test that monkeypatches `claude.extract` with a fake that loops on `cancelled.wait(0.1)` and raises when set; open `/extract/stream` with `client.stream(...)`, read two events, close the stream, and assert the fake observed the cancel within a second.

- **Status:** Open (first seen 2026-10-31)
- **Where:** `/Users/djsiry/GitHub/underwriting-desktop/web/src/lib/login-events.ts:83-86` (`loginReport`: the `missing` query and `Promise.all(... fillGeo ...)` before the report is built), `:52-64` (`lookupGeo` writes `geo_source = "ipwho.is: <message>"` on `success:false` and `"ipwho.is unreachable (…)"` on a timeout, both with `geo = null`), `:10` (`GEO_TIMEOUT_MS = 2_500`); callers `/Users/djsiry/GitHub/underwriting-desktop/web/src/app/audit/logins/page.tsx:82` and `/Users/djsiry/GitHub/underwriting-desktop/web/src/app/api/reports/logins/route.ts:29`

### CR-026 — Web DB pools have no connection timeout, so health, pages and sign-in itself hang when Postgres is unreachable
- **Status:** Open (first seen 2026-10-23)
- **Where:** `/Users/djsiry/GitHub/underwriting-desktop/web/src/lib/db.ts:17-20`, `/Users/djsiry/GitHub/underwriting-desktop/web/src/lib/health.ts:6-13`; on the sign-in path at `/Users/djsiry/GitHub/underwriting-desktop/web/src/app/signin/actions.ts:26`
- **Problem:** `new Pool({ connectionString })` uses defaults (no `connectionTimeoutMillis`, no `statement_timeout`); `checkDb` has no abort signal unlike `checkService` (15 s), so `/api/health` waits on the TCP stack when the database is unreachable. `signInAction` awaits an INSERT into the policy DB before issuing the cookie (the failure is caught, but the wait is not bounded), so a policy-DB outage turns every sign-in into a hang.
- **Evidence:** `customer: new Pool({ connectionString: urls.customer })`; `grep -n "connectionTimeoutMillis\|statement_timeout" web/src/lib/db.ts` → nothing (re-run this run).
- **Fix:** `new Pool({ connectionString, connectionTimeoutMillis: 5000, statement_timeout: 30000 })` for both pools; optionally race `checkDb` with `AbortSignal.timeout(3000)`, and in `signInAction` run `recordLogin` via `after()`.
- **Verify:** Point `POLICY_DATABASE_URL` at a non-routable address; `/api/health` returns 503 within ~5 s and a sign-in completes (with a logged error) within the same bound.

### CR-063 — `contentDisposition` emits `'`, `(`, `)` and `*` unencoded inside `filename*=UTF-8''…`, which RFC 8187 requires to be percent-encoded
- **Status:** Open (first seen 2026-10-29)
- **Where:** `/Users/djsiry/GitHub/underwriting-desktop/web/src/lib/http.ts:7-10`; used by the document, quote PDF, memo, policy PDF, accounting export, sign-in CSV and `gl-http.ts:32-36` responses
- **Problem:** The extended parameter is built with `encodeURIComponent(filename)`, which leaves `-_.!~*'()` unescaped; RFC 8187 §3.2.1 restricts `attr-char` and `'` is the `ext-value` delimiter. A broker file named `O'Brien (final).pdf` therefore produces a non-conformant header whose value contains the `'` delimiter; parser behaviour on it is client-dependent.
- **Evidence:** `encodeURIComponent("O'Brien (final)*.pdf")` → `O'Brien%20(final)*.pdf`; `http.test.ts` exercises only an en dash and double quotes (re-read this run).
- **Fix:** `const ext = encodeURIComponent(filename).replace(/[!'()*]/g, (c) => \`%${c.charCodeAt(0).toString(16).toUpperCase()}\`);` and use `ext` in the template.
- **Verify:** Add to `http.test.ts`: `contentDisposition("O'Brien (final)*.pdf", "inline")` ends with `filename*=UTF-8''O%27Brien%20%28final%29%2A.pdf`.

### CR-094 — `DISPLAY_TZ` is never validated: a misspelt value throws `RangeError` on every page that formats a time, and the web forwards it as `tz=` to rating endpoints whose regex passes unknown zones to `AT TIME ZONE` for a 500
- **Status:** New
- **Where:** `/Users/djsiry/GitHub/underwriting-desktop/web/src/lib/time.ts:6,9-13,16-19` (`DISPLAY_TIME_ZONE = process.env.DISPLAY_TZ || …`, `toLocaleString({ timeZone })`), used by `components/ui.tsx:45` and so by every list, the desk, the workbench, the audit page; `/Users/djsiry/GitHub/underwriting-desktop/web/src/lib/timeline-merge.ts:130-132` (`dayIn`); `/Users/djsiry/GitHub/underwriting-desktop/web/src/lib/timeline.ts:79,83-87` (`qs.set("tz", DISPLAY_TIME_ZONE)` and `AT TIME ZONE $4`); `/Users/djsiry/GitHub/underwriting-desktop/services/rating/app/main.py:181,187,195` (`_TZ = r"^[A-Za-z_]+(/[A-Za-z_+\-0-9]+)*$"`) and `/Users/djsiry/GitHub/underwriting-desktop/services/rating/app/repository.py:67-68,239-240` (`AT TIME ZONE %(tz)s`); the rating admin already guards itself at `/Users/djsiry/GitHub/underwriting-desktop/services/rating/app/admin.py:84-89`
- **Problem:** `DISPLAY_TZ` is a documented, operator-set variable (compose and `.env.example`). The rating admin's `display_tz()` falls back to UTC on `ZoneInfoNotFoundError`, but the web app passes the raw string to `Intl`, and V8 throws `RangeError: Invalid time zone specified` for anything not in the tz database (`America/NewYork`, `EST5EDT ` with a stray space, `Not/AZone`). Because `when()` runs during render on nearly every page, one typo in the Fly env takes the whole desk to the error boundary. The same value is sent to the rating service's `/ratings` and `/rate-table-audit` as `tz=`, where the regex admits it and Postgres raises `time zone "…" not recognized`, an unhandled 500; the audit page then shows "Rating service events unavailable (HTTP 500)" with no hint that the cause is configuration. `test_api.py:85` only checks that `;drop` is refused by the regex, not that a well-formed unknown zone is handled.
- **Evidence:** `node -e 'new Date().toLocaleString("en-US",{timeZone:"Not/AZone"})'` → `RangeError: Invalid time zone specified: Not/AZone` (run this run); `tz: str = Query("UTC", pattern=_TZ)` with no `ZoneInfo` check; `DISPLAY_TZ: ${DISPLAY_TZ:-America/New_York}` in `docker-compose.yml:21,54`.
- **Fix:** In `time.ts` resolve the zone once: `const DISPLAY_TIME_ZONE = (() => { const z = process.env.DISPLAY_TZ || "America/New_York"; try { new Intl.DateTimeFormat("en-US", { timeZone: z }); return z; } catch { console.error(\`DISPLAY_TZ "${z}" is not a time zone; using America/New_York\`); return "America/New_York"; } })();`. In the rating service validate `tz` with `zoneinfo.ZoneInfo(tz)` in the two endpoints (422 on `ZoneInfoNotFoundError`) and parse `since`/`until` with `datetime.fromisoformat` (422 on `ValueError`, see CR-068).
- **Verify:** `DISPLAY_TZ=Not/AZone npm run dev` renders `/` and `/audit` (times in New York, one console error); `curl -i '<rating>/ratings?tz=Not/AZone'` → 422; `test_api.py` gains a case for `tz=America/Nowhere`.

### CR-095 — The audit trail's "Older →" paging and cap notice cover only UW Desktop rows: rating and rate-admin rows repeat on every page, their 500-row cap is silent, the page boundary is by `id` while the list is sorted by time, and `?correlation=` still filters after the cap
- **Status:** New
- **Where:** `/Users/djsiry/GitHub/underwriting-desktop/web/src/lib/timeline.ts:10,70-91` (`before` applied only to `audit_events`; `ratingApi` calls carry only `since`/`until`/`limit`), `:93-99` (`capped: !submissionId && desktopRows.length >= LIMIT`, `oldestDesktopAt` from the lowest `id`), `/Users/djsiry/GitHub/underwriting-desktop/web/src/app/audit/page.tsx:43-44,113-121` (the banner and the `before` link; `applyFilters(all, params)` with `correlation`)
- **Problem:** UX-044 pushed From/To into the queries and added a cursor, but only for the desktop source. On `/audit?before=<id>` the rating log and rate-table audit are fetched again with the same window and `limit=500`, so the newest 500 rating rows appear on page 1, page 2 and every later page while desktop rows advance; a reader paging back through a seeded instance sees the same "Rated …" cards repeated. `capped` is true only when the desktop source hits 500, so a day range with more than 500 rating calls (the seeded history alone has ~100 per month) is cut with no notice. The desktop query is ordered and paged by `id` but the page is sorted by `occurred_at`; with back-dated seeded rows (`id` order ≠ time order) the banner's "events before <oldestDesktopAt> are not on this page" names the time of the lowest id, not the oldest time shown, and a time window can be split across pages. `?correlation=` (the link every Accounting journal and the GL API emit) is still applied in memory after the cap, so an old journal's "UW action →" can land on "No events match" with the cap banner.
- **Evidence:** `ratingApi<RatingRow>(\`/ratings?${qs}\`, warnings)` where `qs` has `limit`, `since`, `until`, `tz` only; `AND ($3::bigint IS NULL OR id < $3::bigint) ORDER BY id DESC LIMIT ${LIMIT}`; `capped: !submissionId && desktopRows.length >= LIMIT` (re-read this run).
- **Fix:** Page all three sources by time: when `before` is given, resolve it to the cursor row's `occurred_at` and send `until=<that instant>` to both rating endpoints (and `occurred_at < $cursor` for desktop, with `(occurred_at, id)` keyset ordering so the page order and the sort agree); set `capped` when any source returns `LIMIT` rows and name which; push `correlation` into the `audit_events` query (`AND ($5::uuid IS NULL OR correlation_id = $5)`) so a journal link always finds its events.
- **Verify:** On an instance seeded with `SEED_HISTORY=50`, open `/audit`, click "Older →" twice: no `rating.calculated` key appears on two pages; `/audit?submission=<id>&correlation=<a January bind's id>` lists its four events; a range with >500 rating rows shows the cap notice naming the rating engine.

- **Problem:** `node --test … src/**/*.test.ts` is expanded by `/bin/sh`, where `**` behaves like `*`; it works only because all 25 test files live in `src/lib/`. A test under `src/app/…` or `src/lib/sub/` would be silently skipped.
- **Fix:** Quote the pattern so Node's glob handles it: `'src/**/*.test.ts'`.

### CR-038 — Serialize startup migrations across instances with an advisory lock
- **Status:** Open (first seen 2026-10-23)
- **Where:** `/Users/djsiry/GitHub/underwriting-desktop/web/src/lib/migrate.ts:6-32`, `/Users/djsiry/GitHub/underwriting-desktop/services/rating/app/db.py:17-29`
- **Problem:** Both services apply `migrations/*.sql` on every start with nothing serialising two processes (`grep -n advisory` on both files returns nothing, re-run this run); `--scale web=2` or a default `--ha` deploy would fail the second starter on `CREATE TABLE … already exists` (now including `policy/008_append_only_logs.sql` and rating `004`), and two web instances would both start the `SEED_HISTORY` run. Latent today (`--ha=false`, one of each in compose).
- **Fix:** `SELECT pg_advisory_lock(<constant>)` on the migration connection before reading `schema_migrations`, including the `CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS schema_migrations`; take a second advisory lock around `seedHistory`.

### CR-043 — Make the compose Postgres healthcheck use TCP so it cannot pass during the init phase
- **Status:** Open (first seen 2026-10-23)
- **Where:** `/Users/djsiry/GitHub/underwriting-desktop/docker-compose.yml:12-15` (also `:60-63`, `/Users/djsiry/GitHub/underwriting-desktop/web/src/lib/migrate.ts:10`, `/Users/djsiry/GitHub/underwriting-desktop/web/src/instrumentation.ts:8-9`)
- **Problem:** `pg_isready -U uw` with no `-h` probes the Unix socket, which the official image's init-phase server also answers, so `rating` and `web` can start before the three databases exist or before TCP is listening; masked for rating by psycopg's `pool.open(wait=True)` retry, but web's `migrate()` is awaited from `instrumentation.register()` with no retry. No `restart:` policy on the three services.
- **Fix:** `test: ["CMD-SHELL", "pg_isready -h 127.0.0.1 -U uw -d rating"]` and `restart: unless-stopped` on the three services.

### CR-061 — The roofing class code `98677` is a literal in two web-tier rules while the rating database owns the class table
- **Status:** Open (first seen 2026-10-28)
- **Where:** `/Users/djsiry/GitHub/underwriting-desktop/web/src/lib/referrals.ts:79-81`, `/Users/djsiry/GitHub/underwriting-desktop/web/src/lib/quote-terms.ts:58`; also `/Users/djsiry/GitHub/underwriting-desktop/web/src/lib/synthetic-risk.ts:97-99`; class table `/Users/djsiry/GitHub/underwriting-desktop/services/rating/migrations/002_seed_rates_2026_1.sql:6-14`
- **Problem:** "Which classes are roofing" is the string `"98677"` in two unrelated web modules (and the test, and the synthetic-risk generator); a new roofing class in a later rate version leaves the manager-approval referral and the roofing endorsement silently not firing.
- **Fix:** Smallest: one shared `ROOFING_CLASSES` set in `web/src/lib/classes.ts`. Better: a `hazard_group` column on `class_rates` returned by `GET /classes` and cached alongside `activeRateVersion()`.

### CR-064 — Declare response models on the FastAPI read endpoints the web tier consumes
- **Status:** Open (first seen 2026-10-29)
- **Where:** `/Users/djsiry/GitHub/underwriting-desktop/services/rating/app/main.py:64-69`, `:84-86`, `:108-113`, `:184-189`, `:192-198`, `:26-34`; `/Users/djsiry/GitHub/underwriting-desktop/services/ingestion/app/main.py:74-85`
- **Problem:** Only `POST /rate` and `GET /classes` declare a `response_model`; the other endpoints return raw `dict`/`list[dict]` rows. The web tier hand-types their shapes (`RatingRow`, `RateAdminRow`, `Extraction`, the `{ id, label }` list in `rating-api.ts:64`, the version list in `assistant-tools.ts:345`), so a renamed column is invisible until a page renders `undefined`.
- **Fix:** Add small Pydantic models (`RatingLogEntry`, `RatingSummary`, `RateVersion`, `RateVersionDetail`, `RateTableAuditEntry`, `HealthStatus`; `ExtractResponse` in ingestion) and pass them as `response_model=`.

### CR-096 — `db/roles.sql` prescribes a role split the apps cannot run, and `scripts/readonly-bash-guard.sh` denies the exact check commands the auditor is instructed to run
- **Status:** New
- **Where:** `/Users/djsiry/GitHub/underwriting-desktop/db/roles.sql:9-12,33-34,47-48,58-59` (the usage instructions and the `schema_migrations` grants); the startup migrators `/Users/djsiry/GitHub/underwriting-desktop/web/src/lib/migrate.ts:6-23` and `/Users/djsiry/GitHub/underwriting-desktop/services/rating/app/db.py:17-29`, which read the same `CUSTOMER_/POLICY_DATABASE_URL` and `DATABASE_URL` as the request path (`/Users/djsiry/GitHub/underwriting-desktop/web/src/lib/db.ts:10-13`, `/Users/djsiry/GitHub/underwriting-desktop/services/rating/app/db.py:10-14`); `/Users/djsiry/GitHub/underwriting-desktop/scripts/readonly-bash-guard.sh:27`
- **Problem:** (1) The script's header says to "point CUSTOMER_DATABASE_URL / POLICY_DATABASE_URL at web_app and DATABASE_URL at rating_app for the request-serving processes, keeping the owner URL for migrations", but neither service has a second URL: `instrumentation.register()` and the rating `lifespan` run `migrate()` on the only pool at every start. Under `web_app`/`rating_app` the first statement, `CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS schema_migrations`, needs CREATE on `public` (not granted; refused by default on Postgres 15+), and the `INSERT INTO schema_migrations` needs INSERT, which the script explicitly revokes, so an operator following the instructions gets a process that fails to start. The build log acknowledges the split is "not switched on", but the script does not say it needs a code change first. (2) The new PreToolUse guard denies `\bnpx\s`, `npm … test|run`, and `uv … run`, which are exactly `npx tsc --noEmit`, `npm run lint`, `npm test` and `uv run --frozen pytest` that the code-auditor's instructions require (this run was able to execute them, so the hook was not active for this session; if it is wired for the scheduled run, every future report will say "checks skipped").
- **Fix:** (1) Add an optional `MIGRATION_DATABASE_URL` (web: `CUSTOMER_MIGRATION_URL`/`POLICY_MIGRATION_URL`) read only by `migrate()`/`db.migrate()`, defaulting to the app URL, and say in `roles.sql` that the split requires it; or add `RUN_MIGRATIONS=0` and a one-shot `npm run migrate` / `python -m app.migrate` command for the owner role. (2) Allow-list the read-only check invocations in the guard (`npx tsc --noEmit`, `npx eslint`, `npm run lint`, `npm test`, `uv run --frozen pytest`, `pytest`) before the package-manager deny line, or carve them out in the regex.

## Resolved since last run
- **CR-069 — A GL push stamps batches outside any transaction, so two concurrent pushes (or a render failure) produce files whose batch column disagrees with the database** — resolved in `aa32db3` (SEC-026): `exportLedger` (`web/src/lib/ledger.ts:207-239`) now `BEGIN`s on a `PoolClient`, reads the rows with `listPostings(f, client, true)` (`… FOR UPDATE`), takes the batch, stamps with `UPDATE … WHERE id = ANY($3) AND export_batch IS NULL`, writes the `gl.exported` event through `audit([...], client)` and `COMMIT`s; the second of two concurrent pushes waits on the locks and then stamps zero. Residual, not re-filed: `renderLedger` runs after `COMMIT`, so a render exception leaves lines stamped and audited with no file delivered; the file is recoverable via `GET /api/gl/postings?batch=<batch>`.
- **CR-070 — `requestOrigin` trusts a client-supplied `X-Forwarded-Host`** — resolved in `aa32db3` (SEC-022/024): `configuredOrigin()` reads `PUBLIC_BASE_URL` (set in `web/fly.toml:13`, overridden by `scripts/fly-deploy.sh:130` for other prefixes) and `requestOrigin()`, `sameOrigin()` and the new `addressedToUs()` use it when present; the forwarded-host fallback now applies only when the variable is unset (local development, where there is no proxy). `http.test.ts:40-59` covers it.
- **CR-082 — The `/admin` proxy forwards the browser's whole `Cookie` header, including the signed `uw_session` bearer token, to the rating service** — resolved in `aa32db3` (SEC-030): `FORWARD_REQUEST = ["content-type", "accept"]` and `FORWARD_RESPONSE = ["content-type", "location"]` (`web/src/app/admin/[[...path]]/route.ts:11-12`); the proxy now identifies itself with the `RATING_ADMIN_TOKEN` bearer and `x-uw-user` instead.
- **CR-059 — The audit page applies its filters after a 500-row-per-source cap, so "From/To" … silently miss older events** — resolved in `d1ea8c5` (UX-044): `loadTimeline` pushes `from`/`to` into the `audit_events` query (in the display zone) and into the rating service's `/ratings` and `/rate-table-audit` as `since`/`until`/`tz` (`services/rating/app/main.py:184-198`, `repository.py:56-71,232-243`), and the page shows a cap notice with an "Older →" cursor when the desktop source hits 500. The parts of the original fix that remain undone (actor/search/correlation still in memory, the cap notice and cursor covering one source only) are re-filed as CR-095.
